newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Greek, Yugoslav foreign ministers sign accord.
newsitem.headline: Greek, Yugoslav foreign ministers sign accord.

text.p: Foreign ministers Theodhoros Pangalos of Greece and Milan Milutinovic of Yugoslavia signed a protocol on Thursday on cooperation between their ministries, the Yugoslav news agency Tanjug reported.
The agency said they discussed regional developments and ways of developing relations and cooperation between the two countries.

Pangalos, who is on a two-day official visit to Belgrade, said on arrival on Wednesday night that particular attention would be paid to Yugoslavia's reintegration into the international community, with emphasis on the process of European integration.
Pangalos said Greece felt that Yugoslavia should be fully reintegated into the international community.
Greece was Yugoslavia's staunchest ally during its 3-1/2-year years of isolation over its support for Bosnia's Serbs.

Greece and Yugoslavia agreed to start talks directed at promoting Greek investments in Yugoslavia, Milutinovic said. They also agreed on further liberalisation of visas for each other's citizens and a reduction of visa tariffs, he added.
Pangalos will meet Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic, Yugoslav Prime Minister Radoje Kontic and Patriarch of the Serbian Orthodox Church Pavle later on Thursday, Tanjug said.
